entries.name: @deepseek-ai/dsh-session-query
comments: # DISABLED — abstract seam: SessionQueryEngine registers ctx.sessionQuery,
# and the sqlite backend below extends it with the SAME service name;
# mounting both crashes on duplicate registration (dsh-jobs pattern).

entries.name: @deepseek-ai/dsh-session-query-sqlite
comments: # ENABLED now that the abstract seam below is installed. Concrete
# ctx.sessionQuery backend with SQLite FTS5 — a retrieval capability,
# NOT a persistence backend (it watches the JSONL store from L2).
entries.configYaml:
config:
    # required: dedicated FTS5 index file — never point this at the
    # JSONL persistence root; the README warns against sharing them
    path: ./sessions/session-query.db

entries.name: @deepseek-ai/dsh-session-reference
comments: # ENABLED: its inject [sessionQuery] is now served by the sqlite backend.
# Cross-session snapshot references as durable (untrusted) model context.

entries.name: @deepseek-ai/dsh-repeat-tool-reminder
comments: # Advisory loop-breaker, not a tool: counts consecutive calls to the
# same tool with canonically identical arguments, keyed per live agent
# (WeakMap — subagents interleaving through the shared registry never
# trip each other), and at the configured run lengths injects an
# escalating reminder as a sourced user message.  It never vetoes or
# rewrites the call.  Defaults kept: thresholds [3, 5, 8], include []
# (track all tools), exclude [] — the README's example excludes
# bookkeeping tools like todo_write so they neither extend nor launder
# a chain — argumentsPreviewChars 500.  In-memory only: a resumed
# session starts with a fresh chain, later reminders accepted.

entries.name: @deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-call-timeout-policy
comments: # Zero-config tools/execute wrapper (inject ["tools"], satisfied by L1):
# arms the per-call budget a tool declares as ToolDefinition.timeoutMs
# on a fused exec.signal and, when its own deadline wins, replaces the
# outcome with a structured TOOL_TIMEOUT result.  Cooperative, not a
# hard kill — a tool that ignores the signal never stops.  None of the
# tools in this composition declares a budget (bash / read / write /
# edit deliberately declare none), so the policy is armed but inert:
# the enforcement point is in place before the first budget-declaring
# tool (the reference examples are web_fetch / web_search) is mounted.

entries.name: @deepseek-ai/dsh-time-context
comments: # Per-step temporal context (inject ["agents"], satisfied by L1): an
# agent/pre-step listener appends one durable plugin-sourced user
# message with the zoned timestamp and the elapsed time since the
# previous model-visible message.  No config: timeZone omitted
# resolves the Node process zone once at load (this headless host
# attaches no browser zone, so the model is told to ask when a zone
# matters), refreshIntervalMs omitted/0 refreshes at every eligible
# pre-step.  Readings are durable session events, so replay and
# resume reconstruct the same timeline without a process-local cache.
